note: Behaviour evals for the recipe. Run them in a throwaway fixture (git-local vcs_host, temp ledger, fake brain); never against a real board.

evals.name: hand-run-tick-reads-dispositions-first
evals.prompt: run the PR review loop by hand once — no scheduler, just do one tick. dry-run.
evals.expected_output: Takes the tick lock, then runs `pr_feed.py dispositions` (without --emit, since metrics were not asked for) before `unreviewed`, puts the one-line dispositions summary in the tick report, and lets nothing in it change which PRs are reviewed. Posting stays dry-run. Releases the lock and tears down worktrees in a finally. Does not claim that waved-off findings are suppressed next time.
assertions: Does NOT pass --emit to dispositions unasked
The report carries a dispositions line
Does NOT post live and does not mark --mode live
Does not claim a false-positive suppression store or automatic suppression exists

evals.name: round-capped-pr-named-not-reviewed
evals.prompt: run one PR review tick by hand, dry-run. I think feature/export is the one that keeps bouncing back.
evals.expected_output: Takes the tick lock, runs dispositions, rounds and step-back --due (all without --live/--emit), then unreviewed. feature/export is under round_capped: it is not checked out, reviewed or marked, and the report has a Round-capped line naming it with its round count and that the step-back was only previewed. Any re-reviewed PR is judged on interdiff_command. The Spend line is unchanged. Releases the lock in a finally.
assertions: Runs rounds and step-back --due without --live or --emit
Does not check out or review the round-capped PR
The report has a Round-capped: line naming feature/export
